main_text.head: Pauperies.
main_text.p: {a}Pauperies autem est damnum sine injuria facien-Quid est pauperies?[illegible, ~2 letters]tis datum. Nec enim potest animal injuriam fecisse dici, [illegible, ~1 letter]ensu caret. Hæc quidem ad noxalem pertinent actionem.

Tertio in §. 2. h. n. definit pauperiem, & ait pauperiem esse [?]n sine injuria facientis datum. Hinc distinguitur paupe-[illegible, ~1 letter]mno per injuriam dato, de quo est lex Aquilia damnum quadrupede datum vocatur pauperies; nec pertinet ad legem Aquiliam; quia lex Aquilia loquitur de damno injuria dato: vero animal non potest videri injuriam facere, cum sen-[?], intellectu & voluntate) careat, nemo enim injuriam fa-[?]olens faciat, ut Aristot. docet 5. Et hic.

page.notes: Left-edge words are cut off by the scan and are marked illegible; the readable parts are kept. Page number reads "693" in an old stylised form, transcribed with uncertainty. The running head is copied as printed, its leading edge fragment omitted. "ædilitio" is read as printed; "ædulitio" is possible. The marginal note "noftram?" may be "noxiam?" and "Au" in note b may be "An". The word "Secunda" is a likely reading of the cut-off word beginning the fourth paragraph. Printed "confumit" is given as "consumit". Printed "docet 5." may be "§.". The line "& l.ult." at the foot right is treated as the catchword. "ff." and "5." are typeset in italic or uncertain form.
